data: First asteroid sample ever returned to Earth — JAXA's Hayabusa survived a hydrazine leak, three dead reaction wheels, an ion engine failure, and a seven-week communications blackout to bring 1500 micrograms of Itokawa material to Woomera AUS on 2010-06-13.

S-type rubble-pile near-Earth asteroid — peanut-shaped, 540 × 270 × 210 m. JAXA's Hayabusa rendezvoused in 2005, made two touchdowns, and returned 1500 μg of surface particles to Earth in 2010 — the first asteroid sample ever returned. Confirmed Itokawa's rubble-pile internal structure: a collection of gravitationally-bound fragments, not a solid body.
Hayabusa — JAXA, 2005 rendezvous + 2010 sample return (first asteroid sample return)
Itokawa is a near-Earth Apollo asteroid — semi-major axis 1.32 AU. Hayabusa's 2005 rendezvous + 2010 sample return was the first NEA round-trip.
Half the longest diameter of the orbit ellipse — and the single number that sets the orbital period.
